questions.q: State the law of conservation of mass.
questions.a: In a chemical reaction, mass is neither created nor destroyed - reactant mass equals product mass.

questions.q: State the law of constant proportions.
questions.a: A pure compound always contains the same elements in the same ratio by mass.

questions.q: Which law says 18 g of water always holds 2 g hydrogen and 16 g oxygen?
questions.a: The law of constant proportions (1:8 by mass).
The smallest particle of an element that takes part in a chemical reaction.
Two or more atoms chemically bonded together - of the same element (O2) or different (H2O).
A charged particle formed when an atom gains or loses electrons - cation (positive) or anion (negative).

questions.q: State the rules for writing chemical formulae using valencies.
questions.a: Write symbols, cross over valencies as subscripts, simplify, and keep the compound neutral.

questions.q: Write the formula of calcium hydroxide (Ca2+, OH-).
questions.a: Ca(OH)2 - two hydroxide ions balance one calcium ion.

questions.q: Why is the formula of water H2O and not HO2?
questions.a: Valencies cross over: H valency 1 and O valency 2 give H2O, matching the 1:8 mass ratio.
